**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Kubenet uses HostPortManager and HostPortSyncer to implement HostPorts and forward traffic to ports exposed from the pods.

Both of them are only working for IPv4, and since they are used only from the kubenet, that wasn't a problem.

It turns out that the code is vendored by other projects, see bug #80810, and fails if is used with IPv6. In addition, the new dual stack feature allows kubenet to work in dual stack mode.

This PR introduces the following changes:
* Kubenet: adds one handle per IP family for the HostPortManager and HostPortSyncer 
* HostPortManager: operates only with one IP family, it fails if receives portmapping entries with different IP families
* HostPortSyncer: operates only with one IP family, skip portmap entries with different IP families

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

issue_context.title: Hostport Manager is not IPv6 ready
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

When creating a pod sandbox which contains host port mappings, then the hostport_manager.go will reject any non IPv4:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8c8c4113f045a00bee611594e402dee07600812b/pkg/kubelet/dockershim/network/hostport/hostport_manager.go#L85-L87

**What you expected to happen**:

That the port gets added independently of the IP version.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. Setup a CNI bridge plugin as follows:
```json
{
  "bridge": "cni0",
  "cniVersion": "0.3.0",
  "ipMasq": true,
  "ipam": {
    "routes": [
      { "dst": "0.0.0.0/0" },
      { "dst": "1100:200::1/24" }
    ],
    "ranges": [
      [{ "subnet": "172.0.0.0/16" }],
      [{ "subnet": "1100:200::/24" }]
    ],
    "type": "host-local"
  },
  "isGateway": true,
  "name": "crio",
  "type": "bridge"
}
```
2. Start CRI-O (current master is IPv6 ready)
3. Try to create the [hostport test sandbox](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/blob/master/test/testdata/sandbox_config_hostport.json):
```
> sudo crictl runp test/testdata/sandbox_config_hostport.json
FATA[0002] run pod sandbox failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to add hostport mapping for sandbox k8s_podsandbox1_redhat.test.crio_redhat-test-crio_1(0fc2e87d7183c0ab0b92a5df7f443eeba92f3735c6c68d06e91d15b1c7ede333): invalid or missing IP of pod k8s_podsandbox
1_redhat.test.crio_redhat-test-crio_1_
```

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): vendored 1.16.0-alpha.1, but it should also affect the master
comments: We should consider that in dual stack mode the rejection would make sense, but if we run a sandbox in IPv6 mode only then the hostport mapping could apply as well, right?

I agree, but in dual stack mode we would not be able to open the port twice for the same interface.

review_comments: comment on the fact that this is safe for valid v4 IPs
these calls are inside a for loop (L458), we can't return, can we?
The iptables interface is different `IPv6` or `IPv4` each one calls a different binary. Shouldn't we load the correct iptables interface here? or is this done early on?
`iptables` interface is received as a parameter, this function is called from the hostport_manager or hostport_syncer methods that only handle one IP family.

`hostportManager.iptables` / `hostportSyncer.iptables` is specifically either an IPv4-only interface or an IPv6-only interface and maybe we should make sure it's the right one? (kubenet is the only user of this code in-tree, and it passes an IPv4-only interface, but I think it also only supports IPv4 pod IPs so that's ok)
I' ve added checks to verify that the pod IP and the iptables version are the same
